newsitem.title: USA: Central Power seeks rehearing on rates.
newsitem.headline: Central Power seeks rehearing on rates.

text.p: Central and South West Corp said Wednesday its Central Power and Light Co subsidiary has filed a motion for rehearing regarding the final order issued on March 31 by the Public Utility Commission of Texas.

The commission ordered CPL to reduce annual retail rates by about $27 million from the level existing prior to the utility placing into effect higher bonded rates in May 1996. It also voted to require CPL to lower rates by about $16 million in 1998 and by an additional $16 million in 1999 through "Glide Path" rate reductions.
CPL in November 1995 requested an increase in base rates of about $71 million a year, CSW noted.

The proposed rate increase was put into effect under bond in May 1996. The difference between the bonded rates collected and the rate levels ultimately implemented is subject to refund to customers with accrued interest.
The commission has until May 15, 1997, to consider the motions for rehearing unless an extension is granted.
Central and South West said the motion for rehearing seeks reconsideration of several issues in the rate case, including:
-- The disallowance of $21 million of affiliated expenses relating to services provided to CPL, by Central and South West Services, another CSW subsidiary.

-- An error in the calculation of a portion of the invested capital associated with the South Texas Project nuclear generating station that was designated as Excess Cost Over Market, or ECOM, and the decision to allow only a 7.96 percent return on equity on the $859 million of invested capital designated as ECOM as compared with the 10.9 percent return approved for all of CPL's other invested capital.
CPL maintains these determinations are not allowed under the state's Public Utility Regulatory Act, the company said.
-- The $16 million "Glide Path" rate reductions in 1998 and 1999 on the basis that these reductions are based upon "single-issue" ratemaking and are not allowed under the PURA.

-- The disallowance of portions of the amount of nuclear plant decommissioning expense that CPL had requested be included in its cost of service. CPL maintains that there is clear evidence that the current funding level is inadequate to ensure full funding of the ultimate decommissioning costs.
CPL also requested the commission revise its final order on other issues, including tax normalization, post-test year adjustments, deferred accounting and depreciation.
CPL's motion noted many traditional ratemaking principles applied in the past were disregarded. "The flaws in the Commission's decision-making are numerous," the motion stated.

Eight other parties, including the Public Utility Commission General Counsel, the Office for Public Utility Counsel, a group of cities within CPL's service territory and a group of industrial customers, also filed motions for rehearing. ((-- New York Newsdesk 212-859-1610.))
